daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Former National Police Chief General Listyo Sigit refused to attend his ethics trial today concerning allegations he authorized wiretapping of the president. The hearing was rescheduled to Monday, 30 November. The National Police confirmed Listyo Sigit cannot resign, and officials stated there is no mechanism to compel his attendance.

  • Vice-presidential candidates Amran and Sugiono underwent medical examinations at RSPAD hospital today, with 25 specialists deployed for the examination, while an MPR verification team monitored the process and separately examined the candidates' wealth reports.
  • NasDem party selected Sugiono to accompany President Prabowo following directives from Surya Paloh, while the Democrat party will study both candidates' profiles before determining its support in the MPR.
  • The MPR will grant a four-day extension if Sugiono and Andi Amran fail to meet vice-presidential requirements.
  • Former MPR Secretary General Ma'ruf Cahyono was charged with accepting gratification worth Rp 30.9 billion.
  • Fahd Arafiq filed a lawsuit challenging his suspect status from the KPK at South Jakarta District Court.
  • Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Dudung will discuss a proposal to change the OPM designation to KEB.
  • An advocacy group stated the MUI formalized KH Ma'ruf Amin's resignation.

Foreign Policy & Defence

An Indonesian Army officer received the highest award at the Joint Forces Staff College in the United States. No other major Indonesia-linked foreign policy or defence developments were reported in today's headlines.

Other

President Prabowo ordered the revamp of Garuda Indonesia into a world-class airline. The Trump administration has proposed new import tariffs of up to 18 percent for Indonesian products. State investment holding company Danantara has invested Rp 162 trillion across energy, food, and hajj sectors.

  • Indonesia is seeking further reductions in EU inspection requirements for nutmeg exports.
  • The government announced Indonesia holds US$5.1 billion in blue economy investment and US$15.3 billion in marine and fisheries investment potential.
  • The Ministry is pushing copyright protection for journalistic works in the AI era.
  • Indonesia is moving to expand vasectomy access amid growing interest, while Baznas and KPAI are preparing a joint program for vulnerable children.
  • Police have identified six bodies from 13 victims of the Pongkor gold mining incident, while Aceh customs foiled an attempt to smuggle six kilograms of gold to Malaysia.
